To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed approach is able to segment 3D point cloud data from a LIDAR scanner into objects moving in the scene, that the approach can be used for the traffic scene understanding of self driving vehicles and that it outperforms state of the art approaches.

we present a method for object segmentation in 3D point cloud data that jointly uses geometrical features and a motion field estimated using a grid based approach to overcome under segmentation and improve computational efficiency by exploiting the sequential structure of the problem.

(1) a sequential distance dependent CRP can be used for motion segmentation of point clouds, (2) the approach is able to handle spatially close objects by utilizing motion information, (3) the method is robust against under segmentation and can be efficiently computed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of new methods for motion segmentation and tracking of 3D point clouds.
the following questions: How to use motion information for object segmentation in 3D LADAR data?
the development of novel methods for the analysis of 3D data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach is able to detect and separate moving vehicles from each other and the background, even if they are very close to each other.
the proposed approach is able to provide a robust segmentation of the data and that the approach is able to deal with the problem of under segmentation in 3D LADAR data.
the proposed method is able to segment the point cloud into objects in a reliable manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel object segmentation approach for 3D LADAR point cloud data that is particularly suitable for the traffic scenario analysis of self driving cars.
we have proposed a novel approach for motion segmentation of LIDAR data that utilizes geometrical features and the motion field of the data.
the proposed method can segment objects even if they are close to each other, which is a common problem for LIDAR based segmentation methods, and it is computationally efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the s ddCRP can be used to jointly model the motion of objects and their segmentation in 3D LADAR data.
a simple motion segmentation approach can achieve very good segmentation results for the traffic scene, and that the proposed s ddCRP framework is very suitable for such a task.
the proposed approach can be used for robust segmentation of traffic scenes in the presence of occlusions and cluttered environments.
